quote: I currently have a small solar system in [the workshop].
stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing small solar system on a separate structure (the workshop) while explaining their interest — this is a depth signal the interest_in_solar item calls for expanding on, but the rep moves straight to 'Okay. Awesome. Sounds good. Perfect.' without asking who installed it, how it's performing, or how long they've had it.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the workshop system irrelevant since the target install is the house, not worth call time.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one follow-up ('how's that system been working for you?') — this is free competitive/experience intel and deepens the interest anchor at near-zero time cost.

quote: I don't want to, I know at some point I'm gonna have to replace the roof on my house, but, I wanna keep keep it clean right now.
stewart_read: Customer explicitly flags a future planned roof replacement on the house — a textbook cross-sell trigger for Ion's in-house roofing team — and the rep responds only with 'Sure. Yeah. Not a problem,' filing it rather than bridging.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep is focused on qualifying the garage as the install target and may be intentionally not complicating the call with a second workstream.
coaching_implication: This is a real miss regardless of intent — even a 10-second bridge ('worth mentioning, we also do roofing in-house, so when that time comes we can look at bundling it') costs nothing and plants a future-revenue seed for the closer to pick up.

quote: Someone else did it. Yeah. Definitely, don't blame me there. Awesome.
stewart_read: Customer reveals they explored DIY solar and wanted cost ideas — a prior_designs signal and a live curiosity hook about what a DIY approach would have cost versus Ion's design. The rep laughs it off and moves straight into bill collection without exploring what the customer found or what cost expectations they're carrying in.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically avoiding a scope-creep debate about DIY costs, staying disciplined per setter_scope_discipline by not engaging on pricing at all.
coaching_implication: Reactive read is more supported here: nothing later in the call returns to this thread, so it reads as filed-and-dropped rather than a deliberate defer. A single question ('what kind of numbers were you seeing?') would surface expectations the closer needs without ever quoting Ion's own price.

quote: About how long does it take?
stewart_read: This is a direct time-constraint protocol trigger. The correct pattern is a firm anchor ('it's a 30-minute call'), but the rep hedges: 'really just depends on, how many questions you have.' That vagueness is exactly what the schema warns increases no-show risk.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may be trying to sound honest/flexible rather than scripted, which could read as authentic rather than evasive.
coaching_implication: Replay this clip — coach the rep to give a confident time anchor first ('typically 30-45 minutes') and only then add the flexibility caveat, rather than leading with uncertainty.

quote: I know at some point I'm gonna have to replace the roof on my house
stewart_read: Beyond the missed cross-sell routing, this line is also a qualification-positive signal: a homeowner planning a future roof replacement on a 22-year residence is a long-tenure customer with a natural timing window for a bundled solar+roofing sale.
coaching_implication: Manager should note this as a lead-quality upgrade for the closer's brief, not just a missed bridge — the customer's own words show planning horizon and stability.

quote: I'll go ahead and get you done for Monday at ten, and then I'll send you a confirmation text with the days I'm in the meeting while I will start with this phone call here.
stewart_read: The rep confirms day/time and promises a text, but the button-up skips the no-driving/computer-readiness instruction and the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake — both required elements per the schema, and the rep's own confirmation line is garbled ('the days I'm in the meeting while I will start with this phone call here'), which risks unclear expectations going into Monday's call.
coaching_implication: Coach a clean button-up close: state day/time, one-hour block, phone format, no-driving/computer instruction, then 'does that sound fair?' — in that order, cleanly worded.
